summary: Twelve validator rules that forbid a key ask Dictionary::get(..).is_some() or list keys(..) rather than table::states, so a forbidden key whose value is a reference to an object the file does not hold is failed as the key: a stream's F/FFilter/FDecodeParms, the catalog's and a page's AA, Requirements, NeedsRendering, the form's XFA, the name dictionary's AlternatePresentations, a page's PresSteps, a configuration's AS, a widget's A and AA, an appearance dictionary's other keys, a permissions dictionary's keys, an image's Intent and a graphics state's RI. table::states' own comment says every rule that forbids a key asks through it.
source: ISO 32000-1 §7.3.10 (32000-2 §7.3.10 in the same words): "An indirect reference to an undefined object shall not be considered an error by a PDF processor; it shall be treated as a reference to the null object." ISO 32000-2 §7.3.7: "A dictionary entry whose value is null (see 7.3.9, \"Null object\") shall be treated the same as if the entry does not exist." ISO 19005-2 sections 6.1.7.1, 6.1.12, 6.2.6, 6.3.3, 6.4.1, 6.4.2, 6.5.2, 6.9, 6.10 and 6.11 forbid the presence of these keys (paraphrased; ISO 19005 is not quoted in this tree).

source: ISO 19005-2 section 6.8 (paraphrased): a file specification dictionary may carry EF only where the embedded file conforms to ISO 19005-1 or ISO 19005-2, and the file specification of an embedded file states F and UF. ISO 32000-1 §12.5.6.15 Table 184: FS "(Required) The file associated with this annotation." (a file specification, direct or indirect).

summary: Colour operators the base standard ignores are recorded as device colour uses: rg and cs /DeviceRGB after d1 in a Type 3 glyph, the same in an uncoloured (PaintType 2) tiling cell, and an uncoloured cell that sets no colour (recorded as the initial DeviceGray) each fail section 6.2.4.3's DeviceRGB or DeviceGray row. The survey carries State::uncoloured and hands it to the grammar only; set_device_colour, set_space and the initial-space record never read it. veraPDF 1.30 reports none of the five (evidence).
source: ISO 32000-2 §9.6.4 Table 111, d1: "A glyph description that begins with the d1 operator should not execute any operators that set the colour (or other colour-related parameters including transparency) in the graphics state; any use of such operators shall be ignored" (ISO 32000-1 §9.6.5 Table 113 the same). §8.7.3.3: an uncoloured tiling pattern's cell is painted in the colour the pattern is selected with. ISO 19005-2 section 6.2.4.3 (paraphrased): a device colour space is used only where a default space or the output intent licenses it.
